stem:
A 27-year-old with type 1 diabetes sees her GP because she plans to stop contraception next month. Her HbA1c is 50 mmol/mol and her BMI is 24 kg/m². She has had no previous pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect. She already takes an over-the-counter pregnancy multivitamin containing 0.5 mg of folic acid daily and asks whether that is enough.

Which folic acid plan best addresses her pregnancy-related risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Continue the 0.5 mg multivitamin, as her glucose control is now at target
options.explanation: Pre-existing diabetes raises neural-tube-defect risk regardless of current glycaemic control, so the usual 0.5 mg dose is not enough.

options.label: B
options.text: Start 5 mg daily now, continuing at least through the first trimester
options.explanation: Pre-existing diabetes is an indication for 5 mg of folic acid daily, started at least a month before conception and continued through the first trimester.

options.label: C
options.text: Continue 0.5 mg now and increase to 5 mg once pregnancy is confirmed
options.explanation: The neural tube closes about four weeks after conception (six weeks’ gestation), often before pregnancy is recognised; the higher dose must already be established.

options.label: D
options.text: Add 5 mg daily only if her HbA1c rises above target before conception
options.explanation: The indication is the diabetes itself, not the current HbA1c; good control does not remove it.

options.label: E
options.text: Take two multivitamin tablets daily to provide 1 mg of folic acid
options.explanation: Doubling a multivitamin still falls well short of the recommended 5 mg and needlessly doubles every other ingredient.

context: Pre-existing diabetes warrants high-dose folic acid before conception and during the first trimester.
